title: "You" Is Not Toxic: How LLM Labelers Rewrite the Web's Conversation Laws
abstract: arXiv:2610.23446v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: What the Web community believes about toxic conversations, such as that toxicity rises in longer and deeper threads, was measured mostly with Google's Perspective API, which is shutting down; large language models (LLMs) will make the next measurements. We find that LLM labelers mistake second-person address for toxicity, and that this one bias manufactures laws that human labels do not show. On 1.25 million news comments with crowd labels, Claude Haiku flags 12% of the non-toxic comments that contain no "you" and 51% of those with four or more; a single crowd rater flags 6% and 10%. Deeper replies address someone more often, so under Haiku toxicity rises with reply depth (+0.93 percentage points per level), while under the crowd's labels it slightly declines (-0.12). translated_title: “你”并非有毒：大语言模型标注器如何改写网络的对话法则
translated_abstract: 网络社区关于有毒对话的普遍认知——例如话题串越长、回复越深，毒性就越强——大多是使用谷歌的 Perspective API 测量得出的，而该 API 即将停止服务；下一代测量将由大语言模型（LLM）完成。我们发现，LLM 标注器会把第二人称称呼误判为毒性，仅这一个偏差就制造出了人类标注中并不存在的“法则”。在 125 万条带众包标注的新闻评论中，Claude Haiku 将 12% 的不含“你”的无毒评论标记为有毒，而对于含有四个及以上“你”的评论，这一比例高达 51%；单个众包标注员的比例则分别为 6% 和 10%。越深层的回复越常称呼某人，因此在 Haiku 的标注下，毒性随回复深度上升（每层增加 0.93 个百分点），而在众包标注下毒性反而略有下降（-0.12）。将“你”改写为第三人称可消除三分之二的虚假上升；仅让 LLM 标记与人群相同数量的评论并不能消除这一偏差，而向 Haiku 展示父级评……
tldr: 研究发现大语言模型标注器会把第二人称称呼（“你”）误判为毒性，从而制造出人类标注中不存在的虚假“对话法则”（如回复越深毒性越高）。
en_tdlr: LLM labelers mistake second-person address ("you") for toxicity, manufacturing spurious "conversation laws" — such as rising toxicity with reply depth — that human labels do not support.
